case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
Lunch net sales rose by $1,751.36 during Lunch 20 compared with the same dates last year. This covers in-store and Square Online orders only, from 11:00 to 13:59 local time. Net sales means gross sales minus discounts minus refunds.

- **Lunch 20 window (Aug 3–30, 2026):** net sales were $34,610.93 from 1,414 completed orders. Gross sales were $40,261.46, less $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 in refunds.
- **Same dates in 2025 (Aug 3–30):** net sales were $32,859.57 from 1,194 completed orders. Gross sales were $34,989.77, less $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 in refunds.

That is about 5.3% more net, or 18% more orders. Gross sales rose by $5,271.69, but most of that went back out as promo discounts.

I used the same calendar dates for last year. Aug 3, 2025 fell on a Sunday and Aug 3, 2026 on a Monday, so the weekday mix differs slightly.

Policy basis: [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] and [Definitions §2, Lunch].

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

reasons: the answer's figures are $2.49, $30.06, $27.57; none is within 3% of $2.64

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as written. I proposed the campaign, and the policy check blocked it. Nothing has been sent.

The blocking reason is the discount size. Texted offers are capped at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves a larger one [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. A 20% offer is over that cap.

You also can't text the whole list. Only customers with verified SMS consent who haven't unsubscribed can get marketing texts. Implied consent, such as giving a phone number when ordering, isn't enough [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. That leaves 943 of your 48,179 customers.

The draft message is: "Mekong Noodle House: Enjoy 20% off your next order, one per customer. Offer expires Nov 5, 2026. Reply STOP to opt out". It names the restaurant, says "one per customer" and ends with the opt-out wording. The expiry is within 14 days [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages; §6, Required Wording]. It would also need to go out between 9am and 8pm local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

You have two options. You can lower the offer to 15% or less, which should pass the check. Or you can approve the 20% yourself as owner, and I can resubmit it on that basis.

case.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?

trace.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
trace.answer:
No. A lead can't approve 25% off. Under [House Policy §4, Discounts], a discount above 10% that isn't one of the standard ones needs a lead, and a discount above 20% needs the owner. So 25% needs the owner's approval.

Two catering rules also apply under [House Policy §6, Catering]. A catering order over $300 needs the owner's confirmation. Catering orders also need 72 hours' notice and a 50% deposit. Seasonal Specials can never be discounted, so they would have to be left out of the 25%.

The policies don't say that being a regular changes any of this. I didn't find a rule giving regulars a different discount limit.
